effects.note: Author effects equal log2 ratios of FPKM group means to 5.2e-14, not fitted DESeq2 coefficients. Registered effect Pearson is 0.9273, median absolute delta 0.0270, maximum 2.0101. All shared author FDR-significant directions agree, but effect definitions differ.

inference.note: The paper names DESeq2. The registered analysis used edgeR-QL and adjusted over 14,172 tested rows, including 21 unpublished rows. At FDR < 0.05 there are 19 author calls and seven published registered calls, with seven shared. All 14,119 effect pairs have literal exported P and FDR. A conservative sensitivity withholds rows with author P = FDR = 1, leaving 14,117 pairs. The deposit does not flag the test status of each such row. The full-list, literal-pair and conservative counts are recorded separately.

coverage.note: The full GEO table contains 22,322 effects. Of 14,151 published registered symbols, 14,119 pair uniquely (99.7739% of output, 63.2515% of author rows). The remaining 8,203 author IDs comprise 7,948 with a single mapped symbol outside the output, 143 without a published symbol and 112 mapping to shared symbols. Table S1 is a selected list.

comparability.criteria: Author-concordance-v2 requires compatible cohort, contrast, features and effect definitions, at least 30 pairs and at least 90% registered-output coverage for a full reference. Either Pearson and Spearman must both reach 0.90, or sign agreement must reach 90% for at least 30 nonzero pairs covering at least 90% of all pairs. Retain magnitude, nominal P, FDR and call sets as context. For Figure 3E apply nominal P < 0.05 and abs(log2FC) > log2(1.5).
comparability.conclusion: For hfd_vs_ncd both effect criteria pass on 99.77% of the published registered symbols. The seven registered FDR discoveries form a subset of the 19 author discoveries. The paper rule reproduces the counts in Figure 3E and, using the Table S1 annotations, all directional pathway counts in Table S3. The selection that produced Table S1 and the biological replication units remain unresolved.

records.summary: HFD versus NCD effects pass both concordance criteria. The published DEG list still requires review.
records.note: The deposited table matches the input SHA-256 in registered provenance. GEO, ENA, the sample sheet and the model identify the same three NCD and three HFD male ARC libraries. The deposited effects are log2 ratios of group-mean FPKM, with zero means exported as 0.001. The registered edgeR-QL effects are coefficients fitted to TMM-normalized counts. Across 14,119 one-to-one pairs, Pearson is 0.92695 and Spearman is 0.92135. Signs agree for 12,891 of 14,093 pairs with two nonzero effects. All seven registered FDR < 0.05 calls occur among the 19 author calls. The historical DESeq2 refit is a separate sensitivity analysis. Figure 3E labels 164 up and 125 down. All 289 GEO features meeting nominal P < 0.05 and an unsigned fold change > 1.5 occur in Table S1. Its ten additional rows pass nominal P but fall below the fold cutoff in both the workbook and GEO. All 230 distinct symbols listed in Table S2 occur among the qualifying Table S1 labels. Using Table S1 pathway annotations, the qualifying set reproduces the up and down counts in all 229 Table S3 KEGG pathways. Including all 299 rows changes 19 of those counts by pathway and adds two pathway IDs. The article reports no original code.

verification.reason: The four published Figure 5b rows were compared in the registered ob/ob-minus-WT direction on normal diet. Two rank-stable directions agree, Npy disagrees, and Ghsr has crossing ranks. Adjusted display values and registered edgeR-QL coefficients quantify different things. The downloadable DE table estimates an interaction.
verification.nextStep: Obtain the Hy DESeq2 group coefficient at the ND reference level, with identifiers, raw P and adjusted P for all rows. The labeled numeric input to Figure 5b and its adjustment history would help trace the Npy reversal and reconcile the Lepr narrative.

comparability.basis: Compare all four authors’ Figure 5b rows using its printed genotype and diet labels and caption’s blue-low to red-high order. Compare the within-gene ordering of normal-diet animal values with the sign of the registered whole-hypothalamus edgeR-QL logFC.
comparability.reference: Ahmed et al., All Life 15, 555–561, Figure 5b (printed p. 560), doi:10.1080/26895293.2022.2078896. The authors’ manuscript.Rmd identifies the four Ensembl features. Their Figshare v1 README and differential_expression.R establish that Hy in doi:10.6084/m9.figshare.18666452.v1 contains the interaction.

cohort.note: The six registered libraries are the full set of GEO Hy/ND GSMs, three per genotype. Their titles and count columns agree, and each BioSample has one ENA run. All six GSMs carry generic heart-extraction wording. The structured tissue fields, count-column names and paper identify hypothalamus. The panel labels genotype and diet and leaves individual animal IDs unlabeled.

contrast.note: For the figure only, take the ob/ob block relative to WT and use only columns labeled ND. Figshare exports (ob/ob − WT on HFD) − (ob/ob − WT on ND), which cannot supply the ND genotype effect on its own.

features.note: All four printed row labels map one-to-one from the authors’ explicit Ensembl IDs to the registered feature map and DE symbols. No identifier substitution or filtering by registered significance was used.

effects.note: Figure 5b encodes DESeq2 variance-stabilized sample expression after successive batch and tissue adjustment. It has no numeric scale. Lepr and Agrp are higher in ob/ob at every corresponding ND rank, consistent with the signs of the registered edgeR-QL log2 fold changes (+0.0780 and +1.2417). Npy is lower at every rank despite its registered +0.8472. Ghsr’s median is higher and its ranks cross (registered +0.2859). The two methods measure different quantities. These observations support an ordinal comparison only.

inference.note: Figure 5b supplies no ND genotype P or adjusted P. Registered raw P is below 0.05 for Npy and Agrp. None of the four has registered BH FDR below 0.05. Author calls and call overlap remain unknown. Figshare P and padj concern the interaction.

coverage.note: All four plotted genes join uniquely. Three have the same direction at every corresponding normal-diet rank. The fourth crosses. The registered fit tested 16,005 rows and publishes 15,859 symbols. The Hy worksheet identifies 17,762 Ensembl rows in the authors’ joint genotype-by-diet fit. It omits the normal-diet genotype coefficient and its P values, so coverage among usable normal-diet tests and overlap of discoveries cannot be calculated.

comparability.criteria: Include every Figure 5b row. Order the three displayed values within each normal-diet group. Assign a direction robust to the unknown color calibration when every corresponding ob/ob rank is strictly higher or every rank is strictly lower than WT. Record the median and any crossing separately. Compare with the unmodified registered logFC sign. Four selected rows fall below the author-concordance-v2 minimum of 30 paired genes, and the display supplies no paired numerical effects.
comparability.conclusion: All four plotted genes were reviewed. Two show rank agreement and one shows a reversal against the registered sign. Ghsr’s higher median agrees with the sign, but its group-mean direction cannot be determined from ranks alone. No fitted normal-diet effect or inferential agreement was established.

The reporting summary identifies the C57BL/6J diet mice as male. The revision protocol describes 16–18 weeks of diet and five mice per pool. Individual GEO records omit sex, exact duration and donor rosters. The pilot GEO records identify one pool of nine female BALB/c mice per arm at 16 weeks (HFHS GSM8635148, standard diet GSM8635150). The authors describe DESeq2 normalization. Figure 3f reports 19 selected linear fold changes, and Supplementary Figure 3h labels additional pilot genes. Applying a single library-size-factor ratio to the two deposited pilot count files cannot reproduce all 19 displayed magnitudes, even allowing for rounding. Figure 3i and Supplementary Figure 3f report overlap counts without gene identities. Supplementary Figure 4d compares diets in activated conventional T cells from C57BL/6J hypothalami. Panel 4g compares Tregs with activated conventional T cells from C57BL/6J brains under HFHS. See SEARCH_LOG.md and refute/check_sources.py in the evidence folder.

verification.reason: Table 1 provides signed Ob vs. C effects and identifies all 54 rows as author discoveries. Exact one-to-one ID mapping pairs 23 with registered edgeR-QL effects. comparability.reference: De la Cruz-Concepción et al., Genes 2026, DOI 10.3390/genes17030297, Tables 1 and 2 and Figure 2. Table 1 enumerates the selected intersection with Ensembl IDs. The Table S1 raw-read column, GEO library records and ENA run reports link the numbered samples.

cohort.note: The paper reports five male C57BL/6 mice per group for body weight and three biological RNA-seq replicates per group. For all nine sequenced samples in Table S1, the raw-read total equals twice the ENA paired-spot count for the corresponding GEO library. The registered fit uses the three vehicle controls C1–C3 and three vehicle HFD mice OB1–OB3 in the whole-hypothalamus track. Table S1 gives 45,716,864 clean reads for OB3 against 42,785,106 raw reads. The raw total independently matches ENA.

contrast.note: The registered coefficient and Table 1 both compare HFD-obese mice with standard-diet controls after vehicle gavage. Orientation is +1. The resveratrol contrast determines membership in the published list. Figure 2a–b and the Table 1 header identify this second contrast as Ob + RSV vs. Ob, although one sentence in section 3.2 labels its 483 genes Ob + RSV vs. C. Section 2.1 starts the four weeks of dosing after eight weeks of HFD. Section 3.1 places dosing in the final four weeks of HFD. GEO’s summary and overall design also differ on timing. The sample matches establish the endpoint comparison despite this ambiguity.

features.note: Only exact author Ensembl IDs with a unique deposited source feature per registered symbol enter the paired analysis. This recovers Snail1/Snai1, Olfr543/Or55b3 and Gm47283/Erdr1y. The Ccl27a symbol belongs to different stable IDs in the paper and deposit. Palm2 contributes to a three-feature Pakap aggregate. Both remain unpaired.

effects.note: Both estimates are signed log2 case/control changes in gene expression. The paper attributes its rounded coefficients to DESeq2 and the registered fit uses edgeR-QL. In the 23 pairs, Pearson is 0.912609, Spearman is 0.869286 and 22 directions agree. Median absolute difference is 0.194968 and the paired RMS magnitude ratio (registered/author) is 0.769399. M6pr-ps changes sign. Using the alternative Ppargc1b value from Table 2 leaves the direction count and policy decision unchanged.

inference.note: The paper reports DESeq2 1.20.0 with BH adjustment. Section 3.2 specifies adjusted P < 0.05 and |log2FC| ≥ 1. Section 2.5 and the Figure 2 caption omit the absolute-value bars. Figure 2a counts 170 upregulated and 223 downregulated obesity genes, totaling 393. The registered edgeR-QL fit adjusted across 20,050 tested features, including 42 unpublished unmapped rows. Zero of the 20,008 published rows meet FDR < 0.05, so the published positive-call lists have an empty intersection. Of the 23 paired author discoveries, zero meet registered FDR < 0.05 and 17 have nominal P < 0.05. The missing complete author table prevents reconciliation of gene membership and testing across the two universes. The published tables supply no numerical gene-level P or adjusted P for a paired comparison. The paper reports HISAT2 alignment and GEO reports Rsubread.

coverage.note: Of the 54 genes in the published obesity/resveratrol intersection, 23 pair (42.59%), covering 23 of 20,008 published registered rows (0.115%). A further 27 map uniquely to symbols outside the registered DE table, three author stable IDs are absent from the deposit, and Palm2 contributes to a three-feature aggregate. All 31 remain in the selected-reference denominator. Table 2 repeats nine Table 1 genes, seven of which pair.

comparability.criteria: Use the printed Ob vs. C coefficient at orientation +1 for every one-to-one pair. Author-concordance-v2 requires compatible cohort, contrast, features and effect definitions, at least 30 pairs and 90% coverage of this selected reference. It also requires either Pearson and Spearman each ≥ 0.90, or ≥ 90% matching directions among ≥ 30 nonzero pairs covering ≥ 90% of the pairs. Magnitude and inference are contextual.
comparability.conclusion: The comparison covers 23 of 54 Table 1 effects (42.59%). Both the 30-pair minimum and the 90% selected-reference coverage requirement fail. Spearman is below 0.90. Directional agreement is 95.65% across 23 nonzero pairs. The complete author results and model inputs are still needed to explain the call-count and coefficient differences.

contrast.note: Both analyses compare two hours of hypoxia against normoxia in mouse hypothalamus. Positive is higher under hypoxia. Liver, DEX, qPCR, ChIP and protein experiments are outside this comparison.

features.note: All 80 distinct labels join one-to-one. Seventy-nine match the registered symbol exactly. Mouse Gene 235493 and MGI:2387648 identify Fam214a as Atosa, and the registered feature map assigns ENSMUSG00000034858 to Atosa. No ambiguous, duplicated or unmatched row remains.

effects.note: The caption assigns every displayed gene an upward author direction. Registered coefficients are nonzero for all 80. Seventy-eight agree. Bcl11a (−0.1816) and Egr4 (−0.0112) are negative locally. Author log2 fold changes, correlations and magnitude differences are unavailable.

inference.note: The caption gives LFC > 0.3 and P ≤ 0.05. The body uses P < 0.05, and the hypothalamic methods specify DESeq2 with 5% FDR. The paper does not identify the P column used for the figure. Of the 80 panel genes, 66 have registered raw P < 0.05 and 33 have registered FDR < 0.05. The response describes Crh as significantly increased. Its registered log2FC is +0.31638, raw P is 0.21230 and FDR is 0.49633. Exact author P values and FDRs are unavailable for paired comparisons.

coverage.note: All 80 labeled rows pair. Both manuscript versions link Figure 5A to 80 genes with a HIF1β promoter motif and report 313 upregulated hypothalamic genes. The peer-review response describes the panel as all genes passing the LFC and P cutoffs. The ratio 80/313 (25.56%) compares published counts. Exact membership of the 313 could not be checked. comparability.criteria: Use every labeled row, its caption-defined sign and the original registered coefficient. The figure has 80/80 paired rows, 80/80 nonzero pairs and 78/80 same-sign pairs. Cohort compatibility remains unresolved, and the figure provides no signed quantitative author estimates for a comparison spec.
comparability.conclusion: Direction agrees for 78 of the 80 author-selected genes. Bcl11a and Egr4 have negative registered coefficients. The selected direction comparison supports the compared closure. Whole-contrast concordance, effect magnitudes and agreement on author significance calls remain unassessed.

comparability.conclusion: Both pairwise numerical routes pass. Full-result acceptance remains limited by 76.63% registered coverage and by the feature dimension, which is rated limited. coverage.note: All 2,301 HTM_High rows have finite effects and nominal P < 0.01. The saved join covers 2,122/2,301 selected rows (92.22%) and 2,122/13,709 registered rows (15.48%). Benjamini-Hochberg reproduces the day-five adjusted P values within 2.89e-15. On the published raw P values, Bonferroni gives 365 calls. At FDR < 0.05 the 14,193 shared tests yield 1,766 author calls and 4,975 registered calls with 1,763 in common. Five further registered calls lack author inference. comparability.criteria: Use every printed Table 1 row. Collapse only exact repeat measurements of the same symbol and join case-sensitively. Preserve EB minus vehicle and printed precision. comparability.criteria: For a full reference, author-concordance-v2 requires at least 30 pairs and coverage of at least 90% of registered genes. coverage.note: Pairs cover 406/431 (94.20%) of the selected S1 reference and 406/10,539 (3.85%) of published registered genes. The author's unlisted P values, FDR and effects remain unassessed.

comparability.criteria: author-concordance-v2 requires at least 30 pairs, at least 90% relevant coverage and supported cohort, contrast, identifiers and effect definitions. Correlation requires both Pearson and Spearman ≥ 0.90. Direction requires ≥ 90% agreement among ≥ 30 nonzero pairs covering ≥ 90% of pairs. All 406 pairs are nonzero. The direction route meets its numerical criteria (99.01%) and the correlation route misses on Pearson. Cohort compatibility lacks the required support. The effects dimension also remains limited because the original DESeq2 design and included inputs are unresolved. The observed slope and the P-value differences are contextual.
comparability.conclusion: The numerical direction criterion is met within S1. Cohort assignment and the precise author fit remain unresolved. A combined correlation pass, full-universe inference and independent replication are unsupported.

records.summary: The paper reports P21 male gene directions. Its methods do not establish the litter-level comparison used by HypoExplorer.
records.note: GEO records nine filtered-air and seven exposed male libraries after Xist-based sex reassignment. Excluding GSM7163652 (OBFH14), as the paper specifies, leaves nine and six. Section 2.4 describes reverse-strand STAR counts, removal of transcripts with fewer than 20 total reads, DESeq2 with apeglm shrinkage separately by sex, and a BH-adjusted P cutoff of 0.1 (strictly less than). The authors report 66 male DEGs. Figure 1B shows group-average expression for selected genes across four sex-by-exposure groups, including higher Ucp2 and lower Ebf2 in exposed males. The figure gives neither numerical exposure coefficients nor gene-level P or FDR values. The RNA-seq methods give no design formula, litter term or aggregation step. The registered edgeR quasi-likelihood model uses reverse-strand count sums within each of three litters per arm and estimates prenatal benzene relative to filtered air. The publisher DOCX and preprint PDF contain CX30 imaging and body-composition figures. All 33 declared GEO sample files contain STAR counts. No author gene-level result reviewed establishes a compatible litter-level effect.
reviewFlags: Sibling libraries came from the same exposure-assigned dams. The published methods leave their dependence in the DE model unresolved. Effect concordance and gene-level inference for the registered six-litter comparison remain unassessed.

Magnitude differences and assay-specific P values are descriptive.
comparability.conclusion: The selected qPCR and registered RNA-seq point estimates agree in direction for Th, Dnm1, Ppp1r1b and Nr3c1. Drd1 and Crh have opposite signs. The six pairs fall below the v2 minimum, and both numerical routes also fall below their agreement thresholds. The study’s original gene-level RNA-seq analysis remains unassessed.

directComparison.note: The 56,943-row author worksheet contains 20,510 finite CBD3 effects and 9,374 finite adjusted P values. Of 11,195 shared effects, 9,343 have evaluable FDR in both results: 13 author calls, one Explorer call, one overlap at FDR<0.1. The other 1,852 shared genes have missing author FDR and are unassessed, not negative tests; none is an Explorer FDR<0.1 discovery. A separate 15-library, same-time model across dose groups reproduces all 13 author discoveries, while a six-library DESeq2 model gives only one. The joint dose-group model, not software family alone, explains the inference difference. Registered Explorer output is unchanged.
directComparison.paperFilterDefinition: Adjusted p-value/FDR <0.1, matching the manuscript. Call overlap uses 9,343 shared genes with finite author and Explorer adjusted P; the 11,195 effect pairs are a different denominator.

cohort.note: The three registered vehicle profiles (GSM8487265–GSM8487267) and three 160 µM profiles (GSM8487274–GSM8487276) match all six H3 columns. N3 uses different profiles. Its N3_2 column matches none of the 24 GEO count files. The paper gives three RNA profiles per arm. Independence of the culture preparations remains uncertain.

contrast.note: Both analyses define 160 µM mogroside V versus vehicle at 24 h, with positive log2 fold change indicating higher expression under treatment. N3 has the registered glucose label and different profiles. H3 has the registered profiles and a different published glucose label. The physical medium for those libraries remains unresolved.

features.note: Join Ensembl IDs by the registered feature map to uniquely mapped output symbols. On each sheet, 11,703 of 11,738 output symbols have a single source feature and a finite paired effect. The remaining 35 combine multiple features.

effects.note: Both report model-based treatment-versus-vehicle log2 fold changes. N3 Pearson/Spearman are −0.07161/−0.10950, with 5,317 of 11,703 signs agreeing and median absolute difference 0.26122. For H3 on the matched libraries they are 0.99943/0.99946, with 11,566 signs agreeing and median absolute difference 0.00694. The glucose label prevents biological sign-off.

inference.note: The authors used DESeq2 and the registered analysis used edgeR-QL. At the paper’s adjusted P < 0.10, N3 has 17 calls (11 down, 6 up) and H3 has 16 (13 down, 3 up), exactly as plotted in Figure 2. Figure 5 and the discussion give 18 for each. Each sheet has zero values equal to 0.10. At adjusted P < 0.05 the author counts are 8 and 5. The registered output has zero calls at either cutoff, so the shared call counts are zero. All author calls have a local test. On each sheet only 2,842 of the 11,703 effect pairs have finite adjusted P on both sides.

coverage.note: Each high-dose sheet contains 56,941 Ensembl IDs. Paired effects cover 99.70% of the 11,738 published registered effects, 49.97% of finite N3 effects and 49.40% of finite H3 effects. The edgeR fit tested 11,763 rows, including 25 unmapped rows omitted from the published output. Filtering, mapping and aggregation limit coverage of the author universe.

comparability.criteria: For a full reference, author-concordance-v2 requires at least 30 paired genes and 90% coverage of registered effects. Either Pearson and Spearman must both reach 0.90, or at least 90% of nonzero pairs must agree in sign, with at least 30 nonzero pairs covering at least 90% of all pairs. Cohort, contrast, identifiers and effect definitions must also be compatible. P values and FDR are contextual. Both comparisons use every unambiguously mapped finite pair in the published orientation.
comparability.conclusion: N3 fails both numerical routes and compares different libraries. H3 meets both numerical routes on the registered libraries, but its published glucose stratum conflicts with the registered contrast. The biological comparison remains unresolved and neither sheet supports an automated same-contrast spec.

features.note: Unversioned Ensembl IDs join 14,269 author features to unique registered symbols. The registered map drops 44 IDs from symbol-level output. effects.note: Author coefficients are precision-weighted differences in log2 CPM, and registered coefficients are differences in mean log2(normalized expression + 1). Positive values indicate higher expression in KO. Across the full-precision pairs, median absolute logFC difference is 0.090795, Pearson is 0.746223 and Spearman is 0.572998. All 14,269 pairs are nonzero and 9,836 (68.93%) have the same sign.

inference.note: The authors quantified reads with RSEM, retained CPM ≥ 1 in at least five samples, applied TMM and voom, and used condition-only limma with empirical Bayes moderation. Registered limma uses eight normalized columns. Its 14,331-row testing family includes 44 unpublished unmapped rows. Every paired row has finite raw and adjusted P on both sides. At adjusted P < 0.05 there are 38 calls among 14,351 author rows and 43 among 14,287 published registered rows. The one-to-one subset contains 37 and 42 calls, respectively, with 29 shared. The additional author call is one constituent of the significant registered Vmn2r29 aggregate.

coverage.note: 14,269 pairs cover 99.874% of the 14,287 published registered symbols and 99.429% of the 14,351 author IDs for the sole registered contrast. The reference is the complete deposited DE table.

comparability.criteria: Under author-concordance-v2, require at least 30 pairs, at least 90% registered-output coverage and compatible cohort, contrast, identifiers and effect definitions. Require either Pearson and Spearman each ≥ 0.90, or ≥ 90% same direction among at least 30 nonzero pairs covering ≥ 90% of all pairs. Use the deposited orientation across all eligible pairs. Magnitude, raw P, FDR and call overlap are contextual.
comparability.conclusion: The pair count and registered-output coverage meet the policy thresholds. Neither numerical route passes, and the cohorts differ. The plot supports the authors’ processed grouping. Animal identity, W15_S83 raw provenance, tissue and strain still require confirmation. No registered contrast qualifies for sign-off.

records.summary: Figure 6 reports 404 WT MBH genes. Its cohort and calling rule require author clarification.
records.note: Study 3 assigned eight male mice per arm and specified daily cagrilintide at 3 nmol/kg for 21 days. The GEO series gives the same dose, while the eight registered treated GSMs say 0.3 nmol/kg. The authors describe bilateral mediobasal hypothalamic (MBH) punches including ARC and VMN. GEO labels these libraries ARC. Of 138 brain samples, 117 qualified for sequencing. GEO lists 116 libraries across the study. CountQC removed two ARC samples across groups, with their identities unspecified. Figure 6 prints n = 6 per group and shows 404 WT cagrilintide DEGs relative to WT vehicle in MBH (96 up, 308 down). The Results and GEO summary restrict the WT zero-DEG finding to DVC and LPBN. The Discussion makes a broader statement about the absence of a treatment effect without specifying how it relates to the MBH bars. The registered limma fit uses all seven WT vehicle and eight WT cagrilintide ARC deposits. The input kallisto files match the registered checksums. On log2(gene-summed TPM + 1), 28,705 symbols were published, with zero at BH adjusted P < 0.05 and 2,985 at raw P < 0.05 (2,146 up, 839 down). Minimum published adjusted P was 0.0643336618892822. The authors used the SUSHI DESeq2App. The sources examined provide no Figure 6 sample manifest, gene identifiers, per-gene statistics or exact DEG rule. Gene-level agreement and author reference coverage remain unassessed.
reviewFlags: If the published n = 6 applied to both WT MBH arms and both came from the deposits, one vehicle and two treated libraries would fall outside the figure. CountQC reported two ARC removals across all arms and gave no IDs. The final per-arm membership is unknown.
The 404 calls lack a Figure 6 statistical rule and gene identifiers. The general significance statement and Figure 7 module-analysis criteria cannot establish which tests counted toward the bars.
The publisher appendix matches the Europe PMC ZIP member and the PMC Open Access copy byte for byte. The same-named BioStudies file contains unrelated respiratory-patient tables.

The indexed February 2025 preprint abstract describes no significant treatment effect across any region in WT and KO mice. The published Figure 6 gives the region- and contrast-specific count. The broader prose supplies no gene-level comparison.

inference.note: Section 2.8 specifies BH FDR ≤0.1 in both tests and |logFC| >1. Table 5’s footnote uses FDR <0.1, and the Figure S2 caption prints FDR >0.1. inference.note: All 16,212 pairs have finite raw and adjusted P values. All 22 author calls and all three registered calls have statistics on both sides. Only Gfap passes both discovery rules. coverage.note: Paired effects cover 95.38% of the 16,997 registered rows, satisfying v2 full-table coverage. They cover 86.02% of the 18,846 author rows. There are 785 output-only and 2,634 author-only symbols. Two tested rows withheld from registered display remain in its BH family.

comparability.criteria: Use the full deposited worksheet, unique author and registered output symbols, and the labelled log2 TRF/ALF orientation. For author calls, Results uses FDR <0.05 and STAR Methods uses FDR ≤0.05, both with logCPM >0. The dataset comparison uses local FDR ≤0.05 on the registered filtered universe. Neither table has a boundary tie. Significance and effect magnitude are contextual.
comparability.conclusion: Cohort, orientation and full-table output coverage are supported. Neither v2 effect route passes. The manuscript/worksheet conflict, historical feature identities and incomplete author testing family require clarification.

cohort.note: Both analyses use P50 laser-captured hypothalamic ependymal tissue from Siberian hamsters. The script removes SPIP19 by name and assigns the remaining libraries to groups by column position. Its six LP, five LPIP, four SPIP and five SP agree with the GEO file labels after exclusion. STAR Methods reports five LP and six LPIP. The registered contrast includes all five deposited libraries from each intermediate group, including SPIP19 (GSM6199271).

contrast.note: Sheet D reports LPIP minus SPIP. Its workbook import names glm_test_LPIP_SPIP_anno_median_cpm1.txt, and its logFC equals the LP-referenced LPIP coefficient minus the LP-referenced SPIP coefficient from sheet A for all 13,345 IDs, to workbook precision. The extraction negates D once. The comparison reads SPIP_minus_LPIP with orientationSign +1. Both groups transferred to intermediate photoperiod at weaning.

features.note: Join the original mouse-projected Ensembl IDs to the registered feature map. Pair a symbol only when it has one input feature. Of 34 unpaired author rows, 23 map to aggregate symbols, 9 lack a registered symbol, and 2 map to symbols absent from the output. The 627 unpaired registered symbols comprise 22 aggregates and 605 without an author feature.

effects.note: Both analyses estimate group differences on the edgeR log2 scale. Across all 13,311 pairs, Pearson is 0.95202240 and Spearman is 0.89977248. All pairs have two nonzero effects and 11,520 agree in sign. Median absolute log2 difference is 0.05284, maximum 0.99076, and the ratio of registered to author RMS effect is 1.00590.

inference.note: The archived four-group script applies median CPM ≥ 1 before TMM and uses edgeR quasi-likelihood tests. It omits the command for D. Sheet D supplies the reported F, raw P and FDR, and BH on its 13,345 raw P values reproduces its FDRs to workbook precision. The registered two-arm fit sums mapped counts sharing a symbol, uses filterByExpr and TMM, and adjusts across 13,948 tested rows, including ten unmapped rows omitted from the public table. All paired raw P values and FDRs are finite. At FDR < 0.05, 494 author and 320 registered genes are called among pairs, with 301 in common. Another three author and 13 published registered calls lack a pair. At the paper’s FDR < 0.001, the full tables contain 114 author and 76 published registered calls, with 74 in common.

coverage.note: Sheet D contains all 13,345 IDs recovered by applying the archived script’s filter to the deposited counts after excluding SPIP19. The registered output publishes 13,938 symbols from a 13,948-row testing family. The 13,311 unique pairs cover 99.7452% of D and 95.5015% of published registered symbols. Each denominator includes all unpaired rows in its respective table.

comparability.criteria: Full-results scope describes the published pairwise table. For concordance under author-concordance-v2, require at least 30 paired effects, at least 90% coverage of the published registered output, and compatible cohort, contrast, identifiers and effect definitions. Either Pearson and Spearman must both reach 0.90, or at least 90% of nonzero pairs must agree in sign with at least 30 such pairs covering at least 90% of all pairs. Evaluate unrounded metrics across all finite one-to-one pairs. FDR < 0.05, the paper’s FDR < 0.001, and nominal P < 0.05 provide context.
comparability.conclusion: The full published contrast was compared. Spearman falls below 0.90 and 86.54% of nonzero pairs agree in direction. The SPIP19 exclusion independently prevents a cohort match. No contrast receives full verification.

effects.note: Both coefficients measure log2 fold change between the same biological states. In the registered direction, Pearson is 0.805081 and Spearman is 0.829910. Among shared genes, 15,088 raw-P pairs and 14,599 adjusted-P pairs are finite. At adjusted P < 0.05, 759 author and 277 registered calls are evaluable in both tables, including 227 shared. One additional registered call, Zfp729b (GeneID 100416706), has missing author adjusted P. Its author call is unassessed.

coverage.note: The complete torpor worksheet contains 16,195 finite effects. The join covers 15,099/15,099 registered genes and 15,099/16,195 author genes (93.23%). comparability.criteria: Use all finite effects from the full torpor worksheet, unique GeneIDs, the code-defined sign and the fixed author-concordance-v2 rules. Require biological and feature compatibility. Treat P, FDR and magnitude differences as context.
comparability.conclusion: The export code and independently labeled count ratios support the sign correction. Both concordance routes fall below their thresholds on the complete published output. The pipelines differ in normalization, filtering and model design. Their individual contributions to the residual discrepancies were not measured. Full verification remains unsigned.

verification.reason: The fit including Arc15 reproduces Figure 2g and the 529 SD1 astrocyte coefficients for glucose versus saline on control diet. For Figure 2g, 5,350 of 9,857 registered genes pair (Pearson 0.976342, Spearman 0.976763, same sign 4,994/5,350). The author calls 34 genes at FDR < 0.05 and the registered output calls zero. Supplementary Figure 5a contains 5,239 ARC/VMH effects from a cross-region intersection. Its 510 genes shared with SD1 all agree in direction, but all coefficients differ and five FDR calls change. The same fit recovers 5,235 of those 5,239 genes with a maximum absolute log2FC difference of 0.206314.
verification.nextStep: Which ARC/VMH astrocyte barcodes, mice, gene filter and edgeR fit produced the .y columns of Supplementary Figure 5a, and which version represents the control-diet glucose response? comparability.basis: All seven registered populations and four contrasts were checked for a matching author coefficient. Direct exact-symbol comparisons cover the three listed contrast IDs in astrocytes, Ghrh neurons, OPCs and oligodendrocytes. comparisons.json records 20 source blocks in those 12 contexts. refit-metrics.tsv assesses mouse inclusion with separate LRT fits to the deposited counts.
comparability.reference: SD1 and SD4 contain nominal-P selections. Source Data 2, 3 and 14 provide the full Figure 2g, Figure 3c Ghrh and Supplementary Figure 6a results, respectively. Source Data 13 contains the ARC/VMH side of a gene intersection with DVC. Source Data 5 and 7 provide selected Ghrh results. Figure 7d reports control-diet and HFD effects for genes selected at control-diet FDR < 0.05.

cohort.note: Arc15 has 25 ARC/VMH astrocytes and received control diet and saline. The nine-mouse Figure 2g refit reproduces all published effects to within 1.077e-10. Removing Arc15 as in the Figure 2c PCA loses ten published genes and adds six. The nine-mouse control-diet glucose refit also recovers all 529 SD1 effects (maximum absolute log2FC difference 4.17129e-10). Arc15 is outside both HFD-only arms. Ghrh refits admitting low-count mice recover both full volcano gene sets. For OPCs under HFD, the paper’s two-cell rule retains Arc30 (3 nuclei) and Arc28 (10). The four-cell rule from the Insr subgroup code drops Arc30 and keeps Arc28. The registered 20-cell rule drops both. The four-cell result is a sensitivity analysis. The original OPC donor manifest is unavailable.

contrast.note: The paper compares HFD (D12492i) minus control diet (D12450Ji) under saline and glucose minus saline within each diet. The registry calls the control diet ‘chow’. Case and baseline agree for all 12 measured contexts. None of the seven HFD-versus-control comparisons under glucose had a corresponding published coefficient in the reviewed sources. The GSE262408 pilot is separate.

features.note: Exact, unique gene symbols within each source block. Eight Figure 3c Ghrh symbols are absent from its registered output. comparisons.json names unmatched author genes. The wider registered and narrower author tested universes are preserved.

effects.note: Both analyses report case-minus-baseline log2 fold changes. Figure 2g has Pearson 0.976342, Spearman 0.976763 and 4,994/5,350 same-sign pairs against the registered output. For the two author control-diet astrocyte glucose tables, all 510 shared effects differ numerically and all 510 agree in sign.

inference.note: The registered output uses a two-arm edgeR quasi-likelihood test. The authors describe robust dispersion estimation, an edgeR likelihood-ratio test and BH adjustment. Figure 2g has 34 author and zero registered calls at FDR < 0.05. For control-diet astrocyte glucose response, SD1 and the regional figure have 76 and 73 calls in their respective tables. On the 510 shared genes, 70 are called in both, two only in SD1 and three only in the figure. Figure 7d itself supplies no P values or FDR. Three of its 40 Ghrh genes lack an HFD effect.

coverage.note: Twelve of 28 contexts have direct comparisons. Full author tables cover 54.28% of registered Figure 2g genes, 83.14% for Figure 3c Ghrh and 94.14% for Supplementary Figure 6a Ghrh. The last clears numeric coverage with a different mouse cohort. Figure 7a has 19 Ghrh pairs, below the 30-pair minimum. The 16 unmeasured contexts comprise all four contrasts for pooled ARC/VMH, pooled neurons and pooled tanycytes, plus HFD versus control under glucose for the four populations with comparisons.

comparability.criteria: Apply author-concordance-v2 separately to each source and context. Require at least 30 pairs and 90% relevant coverage, using the registered universe for full tables and the stated author reference for selected lists. Require compatible cohort, contrast, features and effects, plus Pearson and Spearman both at least 0.90 or at least 90% same direction among at least 30 nonzero pairs covering at least 90% of all pairs. Inference and magnitude differences are contextual.
comparability.conclusion: Including Arc15 is strongly supported by reconstruction of Figure 2g and the selected SD1 control-diet astrocyte glucose effects. Figure 2g clears the effect-correlation and direction thresholds but covers only 54.28% of the registered table. All 513 SD1 HFD astrocyte glucose effects pair and agree in direction within that nominal-P list (Pearson 0.979501, Spearman 0.974294). The two author control-diet glucose tables still require fit provenance. Dataset-wide concordance and full-verification sign-off remain unestablished.

cohort.note: The paper sampled four-week-old mouse hypothalamus from both strains and treated each mouse as a replicate. All 20 registered GSMs, tissue, age, sex, strain and animal labels reconcile to GEO, with five mice of each sex per strain. The coefficient lists omit GSMs. The paper describes related litters, including one litter for the four-week island males.

contrast.note: Both measure the island-minus-WSB difference across sexes in four-week whole hypothalamus. The paper averages sex-specific log2 contrasts from a strain-by-sex model. The registered additive model estimates a common strain effect adjusted for sex in the balanced cohort. Positive values indicate higher expression in Gough mice throughout.

features.note: The join used Ensembl gene IDs across author tables. Each of the 431 pairs has a unique identical count profile across all 20 GSMs in the registered input and canonical matrix, plus a corroborating author or MGI symbol. Of 59 unpaired IDs, 56 match a canonical profile without a published coefficient. Cd209f and Gm9945 also lack a published coefficient. Eno1 has a published coefficient, but its canonical count profile differs from the individual author feature.

effects.note: Both effects use log2 units and positive values for higher expression in Gough mice. Pearson r = 0.9895, Spearman rho = 0.9773 and median absolute log2 difference = 0.02372. Of 431 nonzero pairs, 429 agree in direction. Lsm8 and Selenbp2 have opposite signs in the two analyses. The sex-averaged and common-effect models can yield different magnitudes.

inference.note: The authors defined DE at BH-adjusted P < 0.05 in a DESeq2 strain-by-sex model before pathway and QTL selection. The registered analysis used edgeR quasi-likelihood on length-scaled counts with an additive sex term. Of the 431 paired author discoveries, 371 meet registered FDR < 0.05 and 60 have registered FDR ≥ 0.05. Of all 3,324 registered discoveries, 2,953 lack a paired effect in these selections. The retained gene lists supply zero numeric author P or FDR pairs. Whole-list overlap remains unknown.

coverage.note: The 431 pairs cover 87.96% of the 490 distinct genes in the selected author reference and 2.77% of the 15,568 published Explorer DE rows. All 59 unpaired author genes stay in the first denominator. Figure 1A reports 4,039 author discoveries, or 21% of detected four-week hypothalamus transcripts. The aggregate count does not identify the complete author tested-gene universe.

comparability.criteria: author-concordance-v2 requires at least 30 pairs and 90% relevant coverage. Either Pearson and Spearman must both reach 0.90, or at least 90% of at least 30 nonzero pairs must agree in sign with those pairs covering at least 90% of all pairs. Cohort, contrast, features and effect definitions must also be compatible. Selected scope uses every distinct selected author gene as its denominator.
comparability.conclusion: Close the direct comparison for these selected effects. Both numerical agreement routes pass on the pairs. Coverage falls below 90%, and full author inference and full verification remain open.
